title: Ki ő? — Asking Who Someone Is

sections.content: Combine ki? (who?) with possessive family words to ask and answer about someone's identity.
sections.title: Asking who

items.english: Who is she? She is my wife.
Who is that? That is my grandfather.

sections.content: For someone actually standing there, use ő — calling a present person az can come across as rude, since az is really the 'that thing over there' word. It's fine for pointing at someone in a photo, though, where you're naming a picture rather than a person in the room — Az a nagypapám (That's my grandfather).
